clue.text: With amount withdrawn, trainee gets wine

indicators.note: withdrawn here means drawn back, so the word for amount is read from right to left

parts.note: a sum is an amount
a cadet is a trainee officer

explanation.surface: Someone's pay is docked, but the trainee still gets a bottle of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscadet is a dry white from the Loire valley in France.

clue.text: Sheep, somewhat stupid, upset by being small

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the whole run is read bottom to top

parts.note: a teg is a sheep in its second year
dim means rather stupid

explanation.surface: A rather dim sheep is upset at being the smallest of the flock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns the whole of TEGDIM round.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective, the word describes something tiny or miniature.

clue.text: Getting one member into heaven is not enough

indicators.note: into says the next pieces go inside the word for heaven

parts.note: the sky is the heavens
I is the Roman numeral for one
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Getting just one member into heaven is a poor showing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something meagre or scanty falls short of what is needed.

clue.text: Father turned up with mother, that's obvious

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up means read from the bottom upward

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
a mother is a parent

explanation.surface: Dad turned up with Mum, which was plain for all to see.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparent means plainly visible or evident.

clue.text: Deserve, , we hear, to get the bird

indicators.note: we hear says the word for deserve is said out loud and the spelling changes

parts.note: to earn something is to deserve it

explanation.surface: Someone who deserves it is getting the bird, or so the story goes.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'get the bird' is slang for being booed, which hides the real bird here.
explanation.definitionFit: The erne is the white-tailed sea eagle.

clue.text: Not quite enough food for seconds

definitions.text: Not quite enough food for seconds

parts.words: Not quite enough food for seconds
parts.note: small baked items that come up short of the word seconds: drop its D and the rest can be rearranged into them

explanation.surface: There was too little on the table for anyone to have second helpings.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue plays on the letters of SECONDS: take away the D and they rearrange into the answer, food that is 'not quite' seconds.
explanation.definitionFit: Scones are small baked teatime cakes, served with jam and cream in Britain.

clue.text: Is impertinent to the chaps

definitions.meaning: to give someone lip or sauce
chaps are the jaws or sides of the face

explanation.definitionFit: To give lip is to be insolent, and the sides of the face around the jaw are also called chops or chaps.

clue.text: Denies it's a heavenly symbol for public officials

parts.note: to deny is to say not
Aries, the Ram, is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: Someone denies that a star sign is the right emblem for civil servants.
explanation.definitionFit: Notaries are officials who witness and certify legal documents.

clue.text: Not the kind of generalisation to laugh and sing about

indicators.note: sing about puts the word for sing around the other piece

parts.note: the clue's opening Not makes this the opposite of laughing, which is to weep

explanation.surface: A broad statement that nobody should laugh at or sing about.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening 'Not' makes 'to laugh' its opposite, a loose construction; 'about' then puts sing round it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweeping generalisation is an over-broad claim that ignores exceptions.

clue.text: it's fat and very wet

definitions.meaning: the fat that runs from roasting meat

explanation.definitionFit: Dripping is cooking fat from a roast, and soaked clothes are said to be dripping wet.

clue.text: Flying insect let another out

parts.note: a bee is a flying insect

indicators.note: out says the letters of let are put out of order

explanation.surface: A flying insect frees one of its fellows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges LET into TLE; the definition is 'another', i.e. another insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A beetle is a further kind of insect, besides the bee.

clue.text: Gold on the plateau? A dramatic scene!

indicators.note: in a down clue the gold sits on, that is below and attached to, the other piece

parts.note: a table or tableland is a plateau
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: Someone strikes gold on the high plateau, and what a scene it makes.
explanation.definitionFit: A tableau is a striking group or picture, as on a stage.

clue.text: Is good at his job and no longer saucy

parts.note: ex means former, no longer so
pert means cheeky or saucy

explanation.surface: He is good at his job and has stopped being cheeky.
explanation.definitionFit: An expert is skilled in his field.

clue.text: In the theatre, medico interrupts spinal operation

indicators.note: interrupts means breaks into, so the doctor goes inside

parts.note: back for spinal, op for operation
DR is short for doctor

explanation.surface: In the operating theatre a doctor breaks into someone's back surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'theatre' suggests surgery, but the definition points to the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A backdrop is the painted cloth hung at the rear of a stage.

clue.text: No eating cornets in business premises

parts.note: off one's food means not eating
cornets are ice creams in cones, so ices

explanation.surface: No eating ice-cream cones in the office building.
explanation.definitionFit: Offices are rooms or buildings where business is done.

clue.text: Appropriate a bit

definitions.meaning: a simple jointed bit for a horse's mouth

explanation.definitionFit: To pinch something is to take it, and the jointed bit in a horse's mouth has the same name.

clue.text: Quarter the age of light

parts.note: N, north, is a quarter of the compass
an eon is an age

explanation.surface: A quarter of the age of light, as an astronomy puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: Neon tubes give the glowing lights of shop signs.

clue.text: Spinning sun orbiting the world brings it to light

indicators.note: orbiting means going round, so these letters surround the world
spinning says the letters of sun are turned about into a new order

parts.note: the world is the earth

explanation.surface: A spinning sun circles the world and makes it visible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spinning' scrambles the star's three letters, and 'orbiting' wraps the result round the planet.
explanation.definitionFit: To unearth something is to dig it up and reveal it.

clue.text: Places for drivers of mixed sex, in the vessels

indicators.note: in says the jumbled letters go inside the vessels

parts.note: boats are vessels

indicators.note: mixed means the letters of sex are jumbled

explanation.surface: Seats of mixed sex in the ships.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed' turns SEX into XSE, set 'in' BOATS. Drivers here are coach drivers, not motorists.
explanation.definitionFit: A box seat is the coachman's seat at the front of a horse-drawn coach.

clue.text: All around the island there's fruit for a greedy man

indicators.note: all around says the fruit encloses the island

parts.note: a gourd is a fruit
the Isle of Man is an island in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: An island ringed with fruit is just the place for a glutton.
explanation.definitionFit: A gourmand is a glutton who loves eating.

clue.text: Unauthorised retreat

definitions.meaning: a cosy corner to withdraw to

explanation.walkthrough: 'Unauthorised' is read as 'no OK', two words run together.
explanation.definitionFit: A nook is a secluded corner, and split in two the letters say not okayed.

clue.text: Watch-tower on twisting rim-road

indicators.note: twisting says the letters of rim-road are wound into a new order

explanation.surface: A lookout post stands on a winding road along the rim.
explanation.definitionFit: A mirador is a Spanish turret or belvedere giving a view.

clue.text: Umbellifer an ingredient of nurse's elixir

indicators.note: ingredient of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A plant is one of the things in the nurse's tonic.
explanation.definitionFit: Seseli is a genus of plants in the carrot family, whose flowers form umbels.

clue.text: Amphibian working with mathematician

parts.note: a newt is an amphibian
on means working, as a machine is on

explanation.surface: A newt is busy alongside a mathematician.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Isaac Newton was the English mathematician behind calculus and gravity.

clue.text: I came right out to Offa's place

indicators.note: out says the letters before it are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: Someone came right out to see Offa's home.
explanation.walkthrough: Offa was the 8th-century king of an Anglo-Saxon kingdom in central England.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercia was the midland Anglo-Saxon kingdom that King Offa ruled.

clue.text: Responded and so were held, nonetheless

indicators.note: held says the shortened words are gripped inside the conjunction

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: read as none-less, so the O, a nought or none, is taken away

explanation.surface: Someone replied, and so the others were detained all the same.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nonetheless' removes O (none) from SOWERE to leave SWERE, which AND 'held'.
explanation.definitionFit: To have answered is to have replied.

clue.text: Windy sort of block

parts.note: a building block named after a light wind, made with cinders

explanation.surface: A gusty kind of building block.
explanation.walkthrough: Breeze here is the cinders the block is made from, but the clue leans on the light-wind sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A breeze block is a lightweight building brick made of cinder concrete.

clue.text: Almost get a seat at the opera

indicators.note: almost says the word for a seat loses its final letter

parts.note: a divan is a couch or seat

explanation.surface: Someone nearly gets a seat at the opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' drops the last letter of DIVAN; the definition is loose, the star you find at the opera.
explanation.definitionFit: A diva is a leading female opera singer.

clue.text: Rebuilding a steel plant

indicators.note: rebuilding says the letters of a steel are put together again in a new order

explanation.surface: Rebuilding a steelworks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' suggests a factory but means a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Teasel is a prickly plant whose heads were used to raise the nap on cloth.

clue.text: Booking for jazz musician's frolic? That's great!

parts.note: a gig is a booking to play for a musician
an antic is a playful caper

explanation.surface: A jazz player's engagement turns into a romp, and a great one.
explanation.definitionFit: Gigantic means huge, enormous.

clue.text: Finch is entering the hide

indicators.note: entering says the word is goes inside the hide

parts.note: a hide is a skin

explanation.surface: A finch flies into the birdwatchers' hide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hide' suggests a birdwatching shelter but means an animal skin.
explanation.definitionFit: The siskin is a small yellow-green finch.

clue.text: Should be white but it's turned red again

indicators.note: turned says the letters of red again are reordered

explanation.surface: A flower that ought to be white has turned red once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reads as changing colour but rearranges the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The gardenia is a shrub prized for its fragrant creamy-white flowers.
